reason: The passage explicitly portrays several elite figures unfavorably: Sanballat becomes angry (וַיִּחַר לוֹ) and very upset (וַיִּכְעַס הַרְבֵּה) when hearing of the wall construction, then mocks (וַיַּלְעֵג) the Jews. Tobiah the Ammonite joins him in mockery and disdain. The text describes these elite officials (Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, Ammonites, and Ashdodites) conspiring together (וַיִּקְשְׁרוּ כֻלָּם) to fight against Jerusalem (לִלָּחֵם בִּירוּשָׁלִָם) and cause harm (לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ תּוֹעָה). Their characterization throughout is uniformly negative—they are antagonistic, derisive, and conspiratorial.
